problem: The sentence 'The system has one solution when nullity is 0, and infinitely many when nullity is positive' is written without repeating the consistency condition. Read on its own it is false: a system with nullity 0 can still be inconsistent (no solution), and a consistent system with positive nullity has infinitely many solutions only because it is consistent.
fix: Write: 'Assume rank A = rank [A|b], so the system is consistent. Then it has exactly one solution when nullity is 0, and infinitely many solutions when nullity is positive.'

problem: The chapter describes three subspaces (row, column, null), but the text calls them 'the four fundamental subspaces'. The fourth one is not mentioned, so a student counting three will be confused.
fix: Say: 'These three subspaces, together with the null space of Aᵀ (the left null space), are the four fundamental subspaces of numerical linear algebra.'
